title: Excavations in Palestine and Trans-Jordan, 1940-2: Abu Ghosh (Qaryat el 'Inab)
author: (round-up; excavation directed by R. de Vaux)
location_note: Area between the Crusader church, the mosque and the modern monastery at Abu Ghosh; no map reference; placed by name.
reading: full (the span includes the map figure on p. 104)
notes: 1944 excavation of an Arab caravanserai of about the mid-9th century (excavators), re-used by the Hospitallers from 1141 and restored in the Mamluk period. Same site as QDAP11-113-abu-ghosh (1941 season); not deduplicated.

features.subtype: spring pool against the west wall, small round basin with kiosk in the court, great reservoir outside the east wall, possibly a lower reservoir under the mosque
features.period: khan built apparently in the middle of the ninth century
features.quote: The water supply of the khan is of special interest

features.subtype: channel from the pool to the court basin and drain for waste water
features.quote: From there a channel led to the centre of the yard

features.site: through the ruins to the mosque fountain
features.subtype: later conduit from a spring south-west of the church, still in use
features.period: after the Mamluk restoration, date 'difficult to determine'; still in use
features.quote: Still later, at a period difficult to determine, a new con- duit

features.site: khan, south-east corner, and the yard
features.subtype: internal cistern linked to the great reservoir (later a latrine and cesspit; 10th-11th c. pottery); cistern on a branch of the late conduit
features.period: ninth century khan, re-used by the Crusaders; the second later than the Mamluk period
features.quote: Yet another cistern situated in the south-east corner of the khan
